sources.title: Federal Reserve and Treasury announce TALF launch
sources.provenance_note: Contemporaneous official facility announcement before cutoff.
claims: TALF launched to support credit to households and small businesses after ABS markets had become severely impaired.

sources.title: Financial Stability Plan
sources.provenance_note: Independent fiscal-authority source; different producer and origin from the Federal Reserve.
claims: Treasury described frozen credit markets and a plan to restart credit through capital, lending, and market-support programs.

sources.title: FOMC statement, March 18 2009
sources.provenance_note: Forward observation only; after T0 cutoff.
claims: The Fed expanded balance-sheet support, including longer-term Treasury purchases, while emphasizing stabilization of financial markets and private credit.

sources.title: Monetary Policy Report, July 15 2015
sources.provenance_note: Contemporaneous official financial-conditions assessment before cutoff.
claims: Investment-grade spreads were near historical averages; high-yield stress was partly energy-related; bank credit grew solidly and lending standards eased.

sources.title: Quarterly Banking Profile, First Quarter 2015
claims: Banking-sector results did not indicate generalized system funding impairment at that time.

sources.title: FOMC statement, December 16 2015
sources.provenance_note: Forward observation only; public after T0 cutoff.
claims: The FOMC described moderate expansion and strong labor-market improvement despite weak energy prices, and began gradual policy normalization.

sources.title: Federal Reserve announces extensive new measures to support the economy
sources.provenance_note: Contemporaneous central-bank policy announcement before end-of-day cutoff.
claims: The Federal Reserve announced PMCCF, SMCCF, TALF and other measures to support market functioning and credit flow.

sources.title: Treasury and Federal Reserve announce joint financing facilities
sources.provenance_note: Independent fiscal-authority source on the same-day policy package.
claims: Treasury provided equity support for new Federal Reserve facilities designed to support households, businesses and credit markets.

sources.title: Treasury statement on expanded Federal Reserve lending programs
sources.provenance_note: Forward observation only; used to discriminate policy-backstop repricing from an immediate fundamental recovery.
claims: The policy backstop was expanded materially, increasing financing capacity to support credit markets and the economy.

sources.title: Monetary Policy Report, February 2006
sources.provenance_note: Contemporaneous central-bank report before cutoff; signal is early deterioration rather than systemic break.
claims: Housing activity had been very strong but showed tentative signs of cooling; inventories of unsold homes were increasing.

sources.title: U.S. House Price Index Report, 1Q 2006
sources.publisher: Office of Federal Housing Enterprise Oversight / FHFA
sources.provenance_note: Independent housing-regulator release on the evidence-cutoff date.
claims: Home prices were still rising strongly year over year, but quarterly appreciation had decelerated to its slowest pace since early 2004.

sources.title: Housing, Housing Finance, and Monetary Policy
sources.provenance_note: Forward observation only; demonstrates eventual mechanism confirmation after a long carry/timing interval.
claims: By late August 2007, credit risk and liquidity strains had broadened materially as the housing downturn intensified.
